# Workforce research and AI education

### Crew Scaler | Selected professional work

Skills-demand analysis, workflow quality checks, and co-authored research on professional upskilling.

</div>

<div class="content-block fade-up">

## 1. Workforce research: deciding what to teach first

**Question.** Which skills should a proposed AI training program prioritize, and how reliable are the job postings behind that recommendation?

**My contribution.** I mapped job descriptions to a common competency taxonomy, compared skill signals across roles, and reviewed what the source material did and did not support. I translated the analysis into recommendations the team could discuss when designing training.

**Judgment.** I treated posting frequency as one input, not a count of unique vacancies or a forecast. When salary information was missing, I kept that gap visible rather than presenting a complete-looking pay estimate.

</div>

<div class="content-block fade-up">

## 2. Lesson production: catching mistakes before handoff

**Question.** How can a team convert slides and speaker notes into a lesson without dropping content or changing its order?

**My contribution.** I prototyped a Python workflow to compare slide order and narration against the source deck. I tested it offline with known mismatch cases and documented which steps still required an end-to-end test in the live video workflow.

**Judgment.** Passing offline checks showed that the comparison worked on those test cases. It did not establish that a final video would preserve timing, layout, and captions, so I kept those as separate review checks.

</div>

<div class="content-block fade-up">

## 3. Public research: professional upskilling

I co-authored *AI-accelerated End-to-End Framework for Rapid Professional Upskilling* with Tam Nguyen and Robert Ogburn. The July 2026 arXiv preprint describes how AI can support knowledge acquisition, content development and verification, teaching, and assessment.

[Read the arXiv preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14044){.project-btn}
